At the 3GPP RAN plenary, the 6G study item defined under RP‑253876 [1] establishes the scope for physical‑layer investigations on initial access, synchronization, random access, mobility, and related aspects. In alignment with this study item, the draft agenda issued by the Chair in R1‑260046 [2] gives the following guidance for RAN1 work: Within this agenda, Item 10.5.1.2 explicitly identifies PRACH design and the RACH procedure as key areas requiring deeper examination. This reflects the broader mandate of the 6G initial‑access study item, which spans synchronization acquisition, random‑access mechanisms, waveform and numerology implications, and operation across both terrestrial and non‑terrestrial deployments. In this context, the present contribution provides technical analysis and study inputs related to PRACH behaviour and RACH procedure evolution for 6G. The goal is not to propose concrete solutions at this stage but to highlight specific limitations observed in NR PRACH, identify PHY‑layer challenges that arise under emerging 6G assumptions—particularly for NTN, wideband, and high‑dynamics scenarios—and outline topics that merit RAN1 study under Agenda Item 10.5.1.2. These include waveform robustness, mapping principles, estimation‑quality requirements, beam/context association, and resource placement considerations in ultra‑wide carriers. By framing these issues, the contribution aims to support informed discussion and direction‑setting within RAN1 as part of the ongoing 6G initial‑access study. In particular, the observations presented here are intended to help structure the early stages of RAN1 evaluation by identifying where NR assumptions break down under emerging 6G system conditions. Moreover, the study items highlighted in this document can assist the group in prioritizing topics that require deeper technical analysis in upcoming meetings.

{"chunk_id":"R1-1706885-001","collection":"ran1_tdoc_chunks","metadata":{"source":["Ericsson"],"tdocNumber":"R1-1706885","title":"Increased PUSCH spectral efficiency for MTC"},"point_id":"7931849292607365354"}
. In accordance with the Work Item Description (WID) [2], one of the areas to be even further enhanced refers to increasing the spectral efficiency of the PUSCH. Increased PUSCH spectral efficiency [RAN1 lead, RAN2, RAN4] E.g. sub-PRB resource allocation, with no less than 3 subcarriers within a sub-PRB allocation. Note: There is no intention to lower the minimum required UE capability compared to UE category M1 as part of this WI, i.e. the UE shall still support a PUSCH transmission of 6 PRBs. In accordance with the above WID’s objective, in RAN1 #88bis several companies have provided preliminary simulation results and technical argumentations supporting their view on which technique should be used for increasing the spectral efficiency of the PUSCH [3-13]. Based on the technical inputs made available for RAN1 #88bis, and once all the main candidate proposals are known, this contribution is intended to provide a technical comparison on the benefits and implications associated to each of the proposals.

Title: LS on Rel-18 WI related to vehicular distributed antenna systems Response to: Work Item: S4SEM Source: 5GAA WG4 To: 3GPP RAN WG1 Cc: 3GPP TSG RAN, 3GPP RAN WG2, 3GPP RAN WG4 Contact Person: Name: Hanbyul Seo E-mail Address: hanbyul.seo@lge.com Send any reply LS to: 5GAA Liaisons Coordinator, mailto: liaison@5gaa.org Attachments: None 1. Overall Description: 5GAA reviewed 3GPP Rel-18 work items approved in RAN#94e and observed that the work item MIMO Evolution for Downlink and Uplink (WID in RP-213598) includes several objectives that are relevant to the vehicular distributed antenna system which was one of the 5GAA prioritized areas indicated in RWS-210360. In particular, 5GAA sees that the following objectives related to the multi-panel transmissions are of such relevance: On these objectives, 5GAA would like to inform that a technical report was published as an outcome of 5GAA activity on the vehicular distributed antenna system. The report can be found in the following link: https://5gaa.org/news/distributed-vehicular-antenna-system/ 5GAA suggests 3GPP RAN WG1 in its study and specification work considers the contents of the report, in particular, Section 5.3 for the requirements and implementation aspects of the vehicular distributed antenna system (summarized in Table 5.3-1) and Section 9 for the analysis on potential specification impact. 2. Actions: To 3GPP RAN WG1: ACTION: 5GAA WG4 respectfully asks 3GPP RAN WG1 to consider 5GAA technical report on the vehicular distributed antenna system in Rel-18 work item MIMO Evolution for Downlink and Uplink. 3. Date of Next 5GAA Meetings:

{"chunk_id":"R1-2603444-044","collection":"ran1_tdoc_chunks","metadata":{"source":["Moderators (Ericsson, MediaTek)"],"tdocNumber":"R1-2603444","title":"Final Summary of 6GR Energy Efficiency Study"},"point_id":"16448027805052834948"}
What additional topic(s) to further discuss? Moderator thanks companies' valuable feedbacks. Four main themes emerged from the open-topic feedback. CMCC, vivo and Xiaomi converged on the need to decide the specific group paging rate value, suggesting 10%, 1%, 0.1%, 0.01% and 0.001% as baseline candidates reused from Rel-16 UE power saving and Rel-18 LP-WUS studies. ZTE raised two distinct technical items: (i) the FFS on the 8RX scaling factor that should be resolved, and (ii) a consistency proposal updating the PDCCH-only BW scaling table (with an additional Γ_Tput≤1/2 column at 200%/400% BW and refined DL-antenna-to-micro-sleep factors {0.65, 0.75, 1.0, 1.4}). Nokia carried forward the micro-sleep lower-bound proposal (≥30 units when scaling applies) and the need to clarify the UL traffic assumption used in the evaluation. These items are noted and suggested to be proposed to the relevant agenda items at a future meeting.

3GPP Awards The 3GPP Awards recognise an individuals’ contribution to 3GPP and just prior to the meeting closure, RAN1 honoured the Working Group Chairs’ decision to nominate Eko Onggosanusi from Samsung for the 2025 Awards. Message brought by RAN1 Chair in that occasion follows. MIMO has been no doubt a core part and main area of innovation of 4G, 5G NR, where Eko has instrumentally served as a RAN rapporteur and a RAN1 moderator for multiple Work Items for completing Rel-13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, and 19 with impressive advancement on time. In addition to his contributions in RAN1, he is an exemplar RAN1 delegate. He is passionate about the work, empathetic to fellow delegates, and has the highest level of technical and character integrity. Now, it is the right time to award his remarkable contributions in the past years while encouraging him with new momentum for even greater contribution to 3GPP community when we are moving to 6GR. Meeting was closed on Friday 13th February 2026 14:25 UTC (excluding post email discussions - see Annex F). Please see excel file attached to this report None

RAN1 started discussion Rel-18 UE features for selected topics in RAN1#112bis-e [1]. In RAN1#113 an extended set of topics will be included, where rapporteur’s input on UE features for each WI will be presented for discussion as well. Hence, in this contribution we provide our initial views on UE features for MIMO evolution WI. Based on the agreements reached so far under the MIMO evolution WI, a skeleton of UE FGs structure is proposed in Table 1 . The Release 18 MIMO is discussing technical enhancements in several technical directions, and it is very likely that the main corresponding Release 18 UE features would be independent of each other. These technical categories are: Unified TCI extension for multi-TRP enhancements Two TAs for multi-DCI CSI enhancements DM-RS Reference signals enhancements SRS Reference Signals enhancements UL precoding for Multi-Panel transmission SRI/TPMI enhancements for enabling 8Tx UL transmission Proposal: consider at least 7 independent discussion areas related to the UE features for Rel18 MIMO. Dependencies between these technical areas can be considered at the point when technical details are agreed. Table 1: Set of new Rel-18 UE capabilities for MIMO evolution Proposal: Consider table 1 as starting point for discussions on MIMO evolution WI.

{"chunk_id":"R1-1802013-001","collection":"ran1_tdoc_chunks","metadata":{"source":["Samsung"],"tdocNumber":"R1-1802013","title":"Candidate spectrum for NR-U operation"},"point_id":"3603137283329258321"}
identify and evaluate technical solutions for next generation wireless systems operating on both sub6 and above6 unlicensed bands. This contribution discusses the following candidate spectrum for NR-U operation: Other Unlicensed and Shared Spectrums The 5 GHz unlicensed spectrum consists of three sub-bands, e.g. 5.17 – 5.33 GHz, 5.49 – 5.725 GHz, and 5.725 – 5.835 GHz, and each of the sub-bands can be further divided into non-overlapped 20 MHz channels according to IEEE 802.11ac channelization. The 5 GHz unlicensed spectrum is of particular importance due to its global common availability and most major geographic areas worldwide have authorized wide bandwidth to provide operations on this spectrum. In LTE Rel-13 and Rel-14, 3GPP established work items on LAA and eLAA to evaluate and specify downlink and uplink operations on the 5 GHz unlicensed spectrum. To guarantee fair coexistence with Wi-Fi operating on the same band, a listen-before-talk (LBT) based channel access protocol is introduced for both downlink and uplink. Clear channel assessment (CCA) is mandatory before occupying the channel and maximum channel occupancy time (MCOT) is introduced to limit the channel utilization opportunity to facilitate fairness. Meanwhile, to satisfy the regulatory requirements, support flexible and discontinuous channel access mechanisms, and reduce the overhead introduced by LBT, several enhancements and refinements to LTE were introduce in LAA and eLAA such as partial starting and ending subframe, interlaced PUSCH allocation, and shared MCOT for uplink and downlink transmission. Some of these mechanisms can remain valid and be considered as a baseline for the design of NR on the 5 GHz unlicensed spectrum.
